name: Turkey Egg
description: Turkey eggs (Meleagris gallopavo) constitute a robust avian reproductive matrix, characterized by a high yolk-to-albumen volume and a dense nutrient payload. The biological architecture of the turkey egg provides a superior concentration of phospholipids and long-chain fatty acids compared to standard poultry options. This product serves as an elite delivery vehicle for neuro-active choline and cobalamin, facilitating rapid membrane repair and optimizing the systemic oxygen-carrying capacity through its bioavailable heme-iron content.
macroIntro: An energy-dense lipid-protein assembly defined by a large, nutrient-rich yolk fraction supporting structural cellular integrity.
microIntro: A potent repository of essential B-complex coenzymes, trace mineral antioxidants, and cell-membrane precursors.

healthBenefits: Neuro-Cognitive Infrastructure Enhancement: Synergistic action of choline and B12 fortifies neural pathways, optimizing signal processing speed and memory retention.
Hematopoietic and Oxygen Dynamics: Optimized iron density directly elevates erythropoiesis, correcting systemic markers of hypoxic fatigue.
Cellular Lipid Membrane Repair: Abundant phospholipids serve as primary substrates for the renovation of compromised cellular bilayers.
Endogenous Antioxidant Up-regulation: Elevated selenium concentrations optimize glutathione peroxidase activity, mitigating chronic systemic oxidative inflammation.
precautionsIntro: Given its nutrient density, proper handling and clinical consideration are advised:
precautions: Microbiological Integrity: High-protein avian eggs are susceptible to bacterial colonization; mandatory thermal inactivation to 74C is required.
Lipid and Cholesterol Monitoring: Elevated sterol content in the yolk necessitates quantitative assessment for individuals with cardiovascular risk profiles.
Proteomic Allergenicity: Individuals with IgE-mediated reactions to avian albumins must exercise caution due to high protein cross-reactivity between poultry species.
